claims.text: OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync(int customerId, List<OrderItem> items) throws ArgumentException when items is empty, builds an Order with Status "new" and PlacedAt now, calls repository.AddAsync and SaveChangesAsync, sends notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed"), and returns the Order.
CancelOrderAsync throws KeyNotFoundException("order {orderId} not found") for an unknown id, otherwise sets Status to "cancelled", saves, notifies "order cancelled" and returns the order.
ExceptionHandlingMiddleware in DonHang.Api maps KeyNotFoundException to 404 and ArgumentException to 400.
OrderServiceTests in DonHang.Tests construct OrderService directly and call PlaceOrderAsync(customerId: 1, items: []), asserting ArgumentException, with no HTTP request, token or JSON involved.
OrderService.cs contains only PlaceOrderAsync and CancelOrderAsync and references no HTTP, DTO or EF Core types.
Reading the sub claim and building OrderDto happen in OrdersController; the empty-items check, setting Status "new" and the notification happen in OrderService.
A service method should take plain input and return a plain result, reporting problems with ordinary exceptions, so it can be called and tested without HTTP.
If a service method took the HTTP request as input, every caller, including tests, would first have to build an HTTP request.
CreatedAtAction in OrdersController.Create produces a 201 Created response with the OrderDto as the body.
